problem: The trusted diff classifier rejects a PR that contains both player-facing files and high-risk technical files under every available class: player-facing falls through to the technical branch, while technical is rejected by the earlier player-facing branch.

decision.rationale: Preserve all existing trusted checks and make class precedence mutually exclusive: economy first, then player-facing, then pure high-risk technical. This matches the existing messages and prevents a valid mixed runtime PR from becoming unclassifiable.

anti_pattern.lesson: Resolve one required class by explicit precedence before validating the declaration.

governance.trust_boundary_change: Trusted diff classification is made mutually exclusive according to explicit precedence economy -> player-facing -> technical. No evidence requirement, required status check, workflow permission, reviewer rule or candidate-authority boundary is removed.
governance.bypass_analysis: A mixed gameplay plus high-risk runtime diff remains player-facing, so it still requires the full player-facing manifest, visual provenance and independent evaluation. A pure high-risk technical diff remains technical and still requires its manifest. The wrapper reuses all other existing checks unchanged.
governance.rollback: Revert the workflow invocation, wrapper and regression test together to restore the previous policy. P1 would become blocked again but no game/runtime state would be altered.

known_limitations: The wrapper is intentionally narrow; a later cleanup may fold the corrected branching directly into check_pr_evidence_policy.py once the repository has a patch-safe migration path.
